csv_project_name: Study for Six Rivers Regional Trail Bridge
csv_scope_of_work: The State of Washington, Department of Transportation, may be seeking a consultant to provide Six Rivers Regional Trail Bridge Conceptual Design Study. This study will develop 10-15% design plans for either a new bicycle/pedestrian bridge, or modifications to existing bridge to support safe and accessible non-motorized travel, at three locations along the Six Rivers Regional Trail in Cowlitz County. The three locations are: 1) Barnes Drive and I-5 at trail mile 4.9 (mile zero of trail starts at the Cowlitz/Lewis County Line); 2) Pleasant Hill Road and I-5 near North Pacific Avenue at trail mile 15.6; and 3) East CC Street over the Lewis River in Woodland at trail mile 40.6
csv_disciplines_requested: Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering, Traffic Design Engineering, Traffic Studies
csv_comments: '* * * ADVANCE NOTICE * * *Project Info: *** Advance Notice ***- WA-16174- The RFQ/RFP package is expected to be available prior to January 1, 2027.- Contract Value may be $110K- IMS requests NO PHONE CALLS, NO FAXES, and NO CONTACT with agency at this time.- IMS will continue to monitor project developments and will update when new information becomes available- The RFQ/RFP package is expected to be available prior to 01/01/2027- IMS requests NO PHONE CALLS, NO FAXES, and NO CONTACT with agency at this time.
title: Study for Six Rivers Regional Trail Bridge
short_description: Conceptual study for three trail bridge crossings along a regional bicycle and pedestrian trail.
project_location: Woodland, Washington, USA; Cowlitz County, at three locations along the Six Rivers Regional Trail
project_scope: Conceptual design study to develop 10–15% design plans for three trail crossing locations along the Six Rivers Regional Trail in Cowlitz County. The study will assess either new bicycle/pedestrian bridges or modifications to existing bridges to provide safe and accessible non-motorized travel. Locations: 1) Barnes Drive and I-5 at trail mile 4.9; 2) Pleasant Hill Road and I-5 near North Pacific Avenue at trail mile 15.6; 3) East CC Street over the Lewis River in Woodland at trail mile 40.6.
services: Conceptual design study; 10–15% design plans; civil engineering; structural engineering; traffic design engineering; traffic studies.
relevance_explanation:
- Pedestrian and bicycle bridge project type is explicitly of high interest to sbp.
- Includes structural engineering and conceptual bridge design, offering an early strategic entry point.
- Three separate crossing locations increase potential structural variety and follow-up opportunities.
- Scope is limited to a study with only 10–15% design, so technical definition is still preliminary.
- Bridge sizes, spans, and structural systems are not yet defined, limiting assessment of complexity.
- One option may involve modifying existing bridges rather than designing entirely new structures.
construction_cost_explanation: No construction cost is stated in the source. Only a possible contract value of 110000 is mentioned, which appears to relate to the consultant study fee, not construction. Useful cost-related information available: three crossing locations, conceptual design only, and alternatives include either new bicycle/pedestrian bridges or modifications to existing bridges.
fee_explanation: Taken from the source comment: contract value may be 110000. This appears to be the anticipated consultant contract value for the study.
references_qualifications: Disciplines requested: civil engineering, structural engineering, traffic design engineering, and traffic studies. No specific reference counts or qualification thresholds stated in the source.

notes: Advance notice only. The State of Washington Department of Transportation may seek a consultant. RFQ/RFP package is expected to be available prior to 2027-01-01.
